name: Socket Outlet (3-Pin UK Type G)
tagline: The 3-pole interface that lets you plug in an appliance — and the reason your board has RCD protection.
terminals: Terminal L/N/E screw-block behind the face
parts: Shutter — blocks the live and neutral holes
Live/neutral pins — carry the working current
Earth pin — the longest, opens the shutter
Terminal block — live, neutral, earth lands
safety: A UK socket is fused or supervised by the consumer unit's MCB, and earth is mandatory for the circuit. Don't 'bridge' the earth with the neutral — the entire protective system relies on a solid earth return.

points.label: Shutter
points.detail: A sprung shield covers the live and neutral holes. It only opens when a plug's EARTH pin presses it — that's why the earth pin is the longest. Children's fingers or a stray screwdriver can't reach the live contacts.

points.label: Live / neutral pins
points.detail: The plug's L and N pins make contact here once the shutter opens. Live (right, shorter hole) and neutral (left) are the current-carrying pair — rated at the socket's 13 A and fused inside the plug for the appliance.

points.label: Earth pin
points.detail: Earth opens the shutter and connects the appliance's metal body back to the protective earth conductor (CPC). Never block the earth hole — a fault will then seek a path through you instead.

points.label: Terminal block
points.detail: Behind the face, three screw terminals: L (red/brown), N (black/blue), E (green/yellow). Strip ~10 mm, clamp firmly, and check the fixing screws retighten the cable in the standard orientation.

points.label: Faceplate
points.detail: The white outer housing holds the mechanism and screws to a back box. It also carries the permanent 'maximum 13 A' marking and (with a socket this deep) the identifying brand/part.
